summary: The prompt over-splits at contrastive connectives ('-는데') and filler-only spans, stripping context that later clauses need for subject/contrast resolution. Far more often, it under-segments: long multi-clause sentences with clear discourse-adverb, temporal, or tag-question boundaries are left whole even though measured alternatives show large free latency gains (up to 0.30) with no quality cost. The system should learn to split after opening discourse markers/interjections and before tag-questions or concluding clauses, while keeping contrastive '-는데' clause pairs intact unless the second clause is truly independent.
